# Brainboxes.IO .NET API

> .NET library for communicating with Brainboxes Ethernet-attached data acquisition and control devices. Supports ED-series (Remote IO), ES-series (Ethernet to Serial), and BB-400 (Edge Controller) devices over ASCII or Modbus TCP protocols.

## Installation

```bash
dotnet add package Brainboxes.IO
```

Targets: .NET 10, .NET Standard 2.0/2.1, .NET Framework 4.8

## Core Pattern

All device interaction follows: **Create → Connect → Read/Write → Dispose**

```csharp
using Brainboxes.IO;

// ED-series (Remote IO)
using (EDDevice ed = EDDevice.Create("192.168.0.100"))
{
    int input = ed.Inputs[0].Value;    // 0=LOW, 1=HIGH
    ed.Outputs[0].Value = 1;           // 0=OPEN, 1=CLOSED
}

// ES-series (Ethernet to Serial)
var es = new ES246("192.168.0.100");
es.Connect();
es.Ports[0].Send("Hello");
string response = es.Ports[0].Receive();
es.Disconnect();
```

## Key Classes

- `EDDevice` — Base class for ED-series Remote IO devices. Factory method `Create(ip)` auto-detects device type. Access IO via `Inputs[]`, `Outputs[]`, `IOLines[]` collections.
- `ESDevice` — Base class for ES-series Ethernet to Serial devices. Serial ports via `Ports[]` collection. Each `BBSerialPort` has `Send()` and `Receive()`.
- `IOLine` — Single IO line (digital or analog, input or output). `Value` (int, digital), `AValue` (double, analog), `Toggle()`, events.
- `TCPConnection` — Ethernet TCP connection. Port 9500 = ASCII protocol, port 502 = Modbus TCP.
- `ASCIIProtocol` — Human-readable text protocol on port 9500. Commands are CR-terminated.
- `ModbusTCPProtocol` — Binary Modbus protocol on port 502. Industry-standard SCADA integration.
- `DefaultSerialProtocol` — Configurable encoding and terminating characters for ES-series serial ports.

## Supported Devices

### ED-Series (Remote IO)
| Device | Inputs | Outputs | Type |
|--------|--------|---------|------|
| ED-588 | 8 DI | 8 DO | Digital |
| ED-516 | 16 DI | — | Digital |
| ED-527 | — | 16 DO | Digital |
| ED-538 | 8 DI | 4 Relay | Digital |
| ED-549 | 8 AI | — | Analog |
| ED-560 | — | 4 AO | Analog |
| ED-582 | 4 RTD | — | Temperature |
| ED-593 | 8 TC | — | Temperature |
| BB-400 | 8 DI | 8 DO | Edge Controller |

### ES-Series (Ethernet to Serial)
| Device | Ports | Type |
|--------|-------|------|
| ES-246 | 1 | RS-232 |
| ES-257 | 2 | RS-232 |
| ES-313 | 1 | RS-422/485 |
| ES-320 | 2 | RS-422/485 |

(Plus ES-346, ES-357, ES-413, ES-420, ES-446, ES-457, ES-511, ES-522, ES-551, ES-571, ES-701, ES-279, ES-842)

## Common Code Patterns

### Digital IO Read/Write
```csharp
using (EDDevice ed = EDDevice.Create("192.168.0.100"))
{
    int input = ed.Inputs[0].Value;
    ed.Outputs[0].Value = 1;
    ed.Outputs[0].Toggle();
}
```

### Event-Driven Monitoring
```csharp
using (EDDevice ed = EDDevice.Create("192.168.0.100"))
{
    ed.Inputs[0].IOLineRisingEdge += (line, device, changeType) =>
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Input {line.IONumber} went HIGH");
    };
    Console.ReadKey(); // keep alive to receive events
}
```

### Analog IO
```csharp
using (EDDevice ed = EDDevice.Create("192.168.0.100"))
{
    double voltage = ed.Inputs[0].AValue;
    // For temperature devices (ED-582, ED-593):
    ASCIIProtocol protocol = (ASCIIProtocol)ed.Protocol;
    protocol.TempUnit = TemperatureUnit.Celsius;
}
```

### Serial Communication
```csharp
var es = new ES246("192.168.0.100");
es.Connect();
es.Ports[0].Protocol = new DefaultSerialProtocol()
{
    TerminatingCharacters = "\r\n",
    Encoding = System.Text.Encoding.UTF8,
};
es.Ports[0].Send("command");
string response = es.Ports[0].Receive();
es.Disconnect();
```

### Modbus TCP
```csharp
var conn = new TCPConnection("192.168.0.100", TCPConnection.DEFAULT_MODBUSTCP_PORT);
var ed = new ED588(conn, new ModbusTCPProtocol());
ed.Connect();
int input = ed.Inputs[0].Value; // same API, different protocol
ed.Disconnect();
```

## Architecture

Three layers: Connection (transport) → Protocol (encoding) → Device (user API).
IO values are cached for `IOLineCacheTimeout` ms (default 10). Reading one line refreshes all lines of that type.
Events are driven by a polling timer. Subscribe at device level (`ed.IOLineChanged`) or per-line (`ed.Inputs[0].IOLineRisingEdge`).
